title: What acme is
body: acme is the platform team's HTTP toolkit: an `App` with routes, options and middleware (`acme/`), a problem-format error helper, generated platform limits, and a small CLI (`cli/`). Standard library only; no third-party packages, ever.

title: How this toolkit adds an App option
body: To add an App option: 1) accept and store it in `App.__init__` in `acme/app.py`; 2) add its name to `APP_OPTIONS` in `acme/options.py` (unknown names raise TypeError); 3) add a row to the App options table in `docs/options.md`; 4) cover it with tests. The team suite checks 2 and 3.

title: How this toolkit adds a route option
body: Route options are passed to `app.route(path, handler, ...)` and stored on `Route.options`. To add one: register the name in `ROUTE_OPTIONS` in `acme/options.py`, add a row to the route options table in `docs/options.md`, and read it where the request pipeline needs it (`App.handle` in `acme/app.py`).

title: Error responses the toolkit answers itself
body: Every error response the toolkit itself produces (limits, timeouts, rejected requests) goes through `problem(status, title, detail, slug)` in `acme/problem.py`, which answers `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457). Never answer `{"error": ...}` for these. Type slugs are kebab-case nouns, e.g. `request-deadline`.

title: Error catalogue review
body: New problem types are reviewed in the weekly API review; add the slug to the review doc before release. The review does not block merging.

title: Platform limits are generated
body: Platform limits live in `config/limits.json`. To add or change one, edit that file and run `python3 scripts/gen_limits.py`, which writes `acme/_limits_gen.py`. Never edit the generated module by hand; read values with `acme.limits.limit(name)`.

title: Standard per-route rate limits are not decided
body: Standard per-route rate limits are NOT decided yet. Product owns them and has not chosen numbers. Do not invent limits; when work needs them, say so and ask.

title: Legacy v1 services
body: Old v1 services answer errors as `{"error": "..."}`. Kept only for those services; not for anything new in the toolkit.

title: Supported Python
body: Python 3.12 and newer. No `typing_extensions`, no backports.

title: Release process
body: Releases are cut by the release manager from `CHANGELOG.md`. Version bumps are theirs; contributors never bump the version.

title: Middleware order
body: `app.use(middleware)` runs middlewares in the order they were added, outermost first. Request logging stays last so it sees the final response.

title: Public API surface
body: `acme/__init__.py` exports `App`, `Request` and `Response` only. Everything else in the package is internal and may change without notice.

title: Request logging
body: The toolkit logs through the `acme` logger (`acme/log.py`), never `print`. Warnings about requests go to that logger at WARNING.

title: Handlers and responses
body: A handler takes a `Request` and returns a `Response`. `Response.text()` and `Response.json()` build the common shapes; set headers on `response.headers`.

title: CLI errors are plain text
body: In `cli/`, errors are one plain-text line on stderr, `acme: <message>`, with exit code 2. Never a traceback, never JSON, never the problem format: the CLI talks to a terminal, not to an API client.

title: CLI commands
body: `acme routes --module pkg.mod:app` lists an app's routes; `acme serve --module pkg.mod:app` serves it with the standard library server. Both load the App with `cli.main.load_app`.

title: Options tables
body: `docs/options.md` has one table for App options and one for route options. Columns: Option (in backticks), Type, Default, Description. One row per option; keep them in registration order.

title: Tests
body: Tests use `unittest` and `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`. No third-party test packages. Test modules are named `test_<area>.py`.

title: The team suite
body: The platform team's suite lives in `teamtests/` and the platform CI runs it. It checks the option registries against `docs/options.md` and the generated limits against their source.

title: Scripts
body: `scripts/` holds maintenance scripts run by hand: `gen_limits.py` regenerates the limits module.
